sessions.title: The recipe list
sessions.goal: Serve every recipe from the JSON store through a route handler and render one card per recipe on the list screen.
teaches: route handlers in the App Router
reading a JSON file on the server with node fs
typing a response with a shared TypeScript type
fetching into React state with useEffect
rendering a list with map and keys

criteria.check: GET /api/recipes returns 200 with a JSON array of the 8 seed recipes
GET /api/recipes returns each recipe with an id, a title, a tags array, a minutes number and a serves number
sc-list renders one card per recipe, 8 cards for the 8 seed recipes
sc-list displays the title, the minutes and the serves count on every card
sc-list renders one tag chip per tag of that recipe on every card

cuts.hint: Read the recipes JSON file from disk and return every recipe in it as an array of Recipe objects.
Send the recipes the handler has back to the browser as a JSON array with status 200.
Ask the recipes endpoint for the list, passing the page query string straight through, and put the array it answers with into state.
Turn the recipes array into one card per recipe, each card a link to that recipe page showing its title, a chip per tag, its minutes and its serves count.

sessions.title: Search and tag filter
sessions.goal: Filter the list by title text and by one tag inside the route handler, and keep both choices in the page URL.
teaches: reading searchParams inside a route handler
case-insensitive substring matching
deriving a distinct sorted list with Set and flatMap
useSearchParams and router.replace
keeping screen state in the URL so a filtered list is a link

criteria.check: GET /api/recipes?q=garlic returns 200 with the 2 recipes whose title contains garlic in any letter case
GET /api/recipes?tag=baking returns 200 with the 2 recipes tagged baking
GET /api/recipes?q=garlic&tag=baking returns 200 with 1 recipe, Garlic Flatbread
GET /api/tags returns 200 with the JSON array baking, one-pot, quick, spicy, vegetarian in alphabetical order
sc-list renders 2 cards and the page URL reads /?q=garlic after garlic is typed into the search box
sc-list renders 2 cards and the page URL reads /?tag=baking after the baking chip is clicked, then renders 8 cards and the URL reads / after the same chip is clicked a second time

cuts.hint: Keep only the recipes whose title contains the q parameter, ignoring letter case, and whose tags include the tag parameter; a parameter that is missing or empty narrows nothing.
Collect the tags of every recipe into one list without duplicates, sort it alphabetically and return it as a JSON array of strings.
Write the text of the search box into the q parameter of the page URL, and take q out of the URL when the box is emptied.
Put the clicked tag into the tag parameter of the page URL, and take tag out of the URL when the chip that is already active is the one clicked.

sessions.title: One recipe in full
sessions.goal: Open one recipe at its own route with its ingredients and its steps, and answer 404 for an id the store does not hold.
teaches: dynamic route segments for pages and route handlers
returning 404 with a JSON body from a route handler
reading the route id with useParams
branching on the response status in a client component
rendering a not-found state

criteria.check: GET /api/recipes/lemon-garlic-pasta returns 200 with that recipe, its 7 ingredients and its 4 steps
GET /api/recipes/not-a-recipe returns 404 with a JSON body holding an error field
sc-recipe renders one row per ingredient, 7 rows at /recipes/lemon-garlic-pasta, each row showing the quantity, the unit and the item
sc-recipe renders every step of the recipe in stored order, numbered from 1
sc-recipe displays the message Recipe not found at the route /recipes/not-a-recipe

cuts.hint: Return the recipe whose id matches the one asked for, or null when the store holds no recipe with that id.
Reply with the recipe as JSON and status 200 when the store finds it, and with status 404 and a JSON body holding an error field when the store finds nothing.
Ask the endpoint for the recipe named in the route, put it into state on a 200 reply, and move the page to its not-found state on a 404 reply.
Render one row for every entry in the rows array, showing the formatted quantity, then the unit, then the item name.

sessions.title: Scale the servings
sessions.goal: Compute every ingredient quantity from the servings number held in React state, so raising the count and lowering it again returns the recipe to the quantities it was written with.
teaches: deriving what is on screen from state instead of from the server
exact fraction arithmetic with a numerator and a denominator
reducing a fraction with the greatest common divisor
clamping a value inside a state setter
scaling from the stored value every time rather than from the value on screen

criteria.check: sc-recipe displays 6 as the servings count after the plus control is clicked twice at /recipes/lemon-garlic-pasta, which is stored as serves 4
sc-recipe displays 3 tbsp of olive oil at 6 servings, where the stored quantity is 2 tbsp at serves 4
sc-recipe displays 1/2 tsp of chilli flakes at 6 servings, where the stored quantity is 1/3 tsp at serves 4
sc-recipe displays 1/3 tsp of chilli flakes again after the servings count is raised from 4 to 6 and lowered back to 4
sc-recipe displays 1 as the servings count after the minus control is clicked while the servings count is 1

cuts.hint: Multiply the quantity by the target servings over the base servings, then divide the numerator and the denominator by their greatest common divisor.
Put the requested number into the servings state, holding it at 1 when it would drop below 1 and at 24 when it would climb above 24.
Replace the quantity of the row with the stored quantity scaled from the serves count of the recipe to the servings count on screen.
